title: Differential and square-zero descent on fixed graded term models
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preorder, $F:I\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ a diagram with colimit $A$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and $P^\bullet$ a cochain complex of $A$-modules (objects $P^n$ and maps $d_P^{mn}$, zero unless $m+1=n$, with all successive composites zero). Fix $i\in I$, finitely presented $F(i)$-modules $M^n$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], integers $a,b$ such that $M^n=0$ for $n<a$ or $b<n$, and isomorphisms $e_n:M^n\otimes_{F(i)}A\cong P^n$. There exist $j\ge i$, maps $d_j^{mn}:M^m\otimes_{F(i)}F(j)\to M^n\otimes_{F(i)}F(j)$, and isomorphisms $e'_n:(M^n\otimes_{F(i)}F(j))\otimes_{F(j)}A\cong P^n$, such that $d_j^{mn}=0$ unless $m+1=n$, $d_j^{mn}d_j^{nk}=0$ for every $m,n,k$, and $e'_n\circ(d_j^{mn}\otimes A)=d_P^{mn}\circ e'_m$. The terms are the prescribed scalar extensions of M; no new term objects or finite-projectivity assertion are supplied.

proof.text: Apply bounded graded map descent to P.X and P.d to obtain a stage j, shape-compatible maps d, and a coherent termwise comparison e prime, without square-zero relations.

The j-stage terms are finitely presented by the tensor-product finite-presentation instance. Compose two compatibility squares and cancel the target comparison isomorphism to prove that every composite d(m,n) followed by d(n,k) becomes zero over the colimit, since P has square-zero differentials.

Index the finitely many adjacent composites starting at degrees m in [a,b]. Apply simultaneous eventual equality to these composites and zero, with source term m and target term m+2, obtaining a later stage k.

For any triple, if one pair is not adjacent its map vanishes by shape. Otherwise the triple is (m,m+1,m+2); if m lies in [a,b] use the imposed equality, and if not, its source term is zero and the first map vanishes. This proves all composites zero after extension to k, including the empty-interval case.

Use the canonical scalar-extension composition isomorphism to conjugate the k-extensions of d into maps on direct extensions of the original M terms. Combine its image over the colimit with the inverse of the comparison for j to k to colimit and e prime. Cancellation proves shape and square-zero, and naturality proves the compatibility squares. Return these maps and isomorphisms without constructing a complex.

lean.statement: theorem exists_differentials_on_graded_model_of_directed_colimit {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I] (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [HasColimit F] (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (colimit F : CommRingCat.{u})) ℤ) (i : I) (M : ℤ → ModuleCat.{u} (F.obj i)) (a b : ℤ) (hzero : ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (M n)) (hfp : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.FinitePresentation (F.obj i) (M n)) (e : ∀ n : ℤ, (ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F i).hom).obj (M n) ≅ P.X n) : ∃ (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j), let G := ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE hij)).hom let E := ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F j).hom ∃ (d : ∀ m n : ℤ, G.obj (M m) ⟶ G.obj (M n)) (e' : ∀ n : ℤ, E.obj (G.obj (M n)) ≅ P.X n), (∀ m n : ℤ, ¬ (ComplexShape.up ℤ).Rel m n → d m n = 0) ∧ (∀ m n k : ℤ, d m n ≫ d n k = 0) ∧ (∀ m n : ℤ, (e' m).hom ≫ P.d m n = E.map (d m n) ≫ (e' n).hom)
